title: Cap. X: Garissoles’s contradiction; Placeus keeps consequent reatus — before Cap. XI
pass_a_gloss: I could also in this place object a contradiction to Lord Garissoles. For he says that if there is no reatus prior to corruption, there is no need of imputed Christ's justice, and yet elsewhere he admits there is an imputation and a reatus posterior to corruption. To this reatus which follows corruption, what remedy answers in just proportion? Sanctification? It is not properly opposed to reatus. Imputed Christ's justice? This therefore, once consequent or mediate imputation is granted, is necessary for us. So the doctrine of imputed Christ's justice is not weakened by Placeus: for he acknowledges consequent imputation and reatus; and thus original sin and the necessity of Christ's satisfaction, and has nothing in common with the errors of Socinians, Arminians, and the like.
pass_b_english: I can also charge Lord Garissoles with a contradiction here. He says that if no guilt precedes corruption, we do not need Christ’s imputed justice; yet elsewhere he admits an imputation and a guilt that follow corruption. What matching remedy answers that later guilt? Sanctification? It does not properly stand against guilt. Christ’s imputed justice? Once consequent or mediate imputation is granted, that justice is what we need. So Placeus does not shake the doctrine of Christ’s imputed righteousness: he owns consequent imputation and guilt, and with them original sin and the need for Christ’s satisfaction — and he shares nothing with Socinian, Arminian, and kindred errors.
source_text: Possem etiam hoc loco contradictionem Domino Garissolio objicere. Ait enim, si nullus sit reatus prior corruptione, non esse opus imputata Christi justitia, & tamen alibi fatetur esse imputationem, & reatum corruptione posteriorem. Huic reatui qui corruptionem sequitur, quod justa proportione remedium respondet? sanctificatio? non opponitur proprie reatui. Justitia Christi imputata? Haec igitur, posita imputatione consequente seu mediata, nobis necessaria est. Itaque non labefactatur a Placeo doctrina de justitia Christi imputata: agnoscit enim imputationem & reatum consequentem; atque adeo peccatum originale, & satisfactionis Christi necessitatem, nihilque habet cum erroribus Socinianorum, Arminianorum &c, conjunctum.

choices.decision: Placeus keeps mediate/consequent imputation; does not share Socinian/Arminian errors
